title: WPSB/169/2010 of VIJAY CHANDRA RATURI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 169 of 2010
Vijay Chandra Raturi. .......... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another. ........... Respondents
Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. A.K. Verma, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. A.S. Rawat, Addl. Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent
No. 1.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Advocate for respondent No. 2.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.

BARIN GHOSH, C. J. (Oral)
 After the creation of the High Court in Uttarakhand, the Chief
Justice, with the approval of the State Government, created one post of
Head Bench Secretary in the pay-scale of ` 10,650-15,850/-. Subsequent
thereto, the Chief Justice forwarded the Rules on 5th January, 2006 to the
State Government. In these Rules, the post of Head Bench Secretary was
upgraded and the nomenclature was altered to Head Bench Secretary
(Grade I). The Rules suggested creation of two more posts of Head
Bench Secretary (Grade II). It was proposed that Head Bench Secretaries
(Grade II) will be entitled to the pay-scale of ` 10,650-15,850/-, whereas
Head Bench Secretary (Grade I) will be entitled to the pay-scale of
` 16,400-20,000/-. The Government, by its letter dated 24th September,
2008, agreed to the proposal, but, at the same time, held out that the
number of posts as well as the pay-scales, as already approved, shall
remain unchanged. Having regard to such response on the part of the
Government, the Chief Justice had constituted a Committee of Judges for
the purpose of going into the question as to whether concurrence of the
State Government has been received to the proposal of the Chief Justice
or not. Two Hon'ble Judges of this Court, so nominated by the Hon'ble

2
Chief Justice, went into the matter and found, upon consideration of the
proposal and the response thereto, that no approval of substantial part of
the Rules has been granted by the Government and that, for not approving
the number of posts and the pay-scales proposed in the draft Rules, the
purpose of framing the draft Rules has been defeated. This opinion was
expressed by the Committee of Judges some time in July, 2009. Since
then, the Chief Justice has not taken any action. But, at the same time, as
was reported by the Committee of Judges that the draft Rules cannot be
notified and enforced, the Chief Justice did not take any action to notify or
enforce the draft Rules.
2. The present writ petition seeks emoluments of the petitioner
treating him to have been placed in the post of Head Bench Secretary
(Grade I), in terms of the proposal that was given by the Chief Justice on
5th January, 2006 and which met its fate from the Government on 24th
September, 2008. The fact remains that, until such time the Rules are
notified, there is no post of Head Bench Secretary (Grade I). Even in
terms of the proposed Rules, there is no provision of automatic elevation
of Head Bench Secretary to the post of Head Bench Secretary (Grade I).
Therefore, even under the proposed Rules, somebody has to apply his
mind and post a person in the post of Head Bench Secretary (Grade I).
This writ petition has been filed at a time when no right of any nature had
crystallised in favour of the petitioner.
3. The writ petition is thoroughly misconceived and the same is
dismissed. It shall only be open to the petitioner to re-approach this
Court, in the event, ultimately, the draft Rules, as were forwarded by the
Chief Justice on 5th January, 2006, are notified.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
 25.07.2013 25.07.2013
G
